scenes.heading: Handling revision rounds without scope creep

sents.d: Handling revision rounds without scope creep
Clear revision limits protect your time without feeling rigid to clients.
Scope creep in design usually happens gradually — a client asks for 'one small change' that's actually a new concept, and without a clear boundary, an entire project can quietly balloon in hours.

Defining what counts as a revision (adjusting an existing concept) versus a new concept (a different direction entirely) in the contract gives you language to reference when a request falls outside what's included.

When a request exceeds the agreed scope, naming it plainly and offering a quote for the additional work — rather than either refusing outright or absorbing it silently — keeps the relationship professional on both sides.

take: Separate revisions from new concepts, and quote anything extra.
